Sydney blocked drain specialists

Drains cleared properly, not just poked and hoped

When a drain backs up you want it flowing again quickly, and you want to know it will stay that way. We are a Sydney blocked drain and pipe relining team working across homes, businesses and strata buildings, and drains are the whole job rather than a sideline.

Every job starts with a proper diagnosis. A CCTV camera goes down the line so we can see exactly what is causing the blockage and where it sits, then we clear it with an electric eel or a high-pressure water jetter. If the pipe itself is cracked, sagging or full of roots, we can reline it from the inside with no digging, or replace the failed section when that is the sounder call.

That order matters. Clearing a blockage in a broken pipe buys you a few weeks. Finding the fault first is what stops the same drain blocking again next season, and it is why we camera-check the line before and after the work rather than only at the start.

What your drain is trying to tell you

Different warning signs point to very different problems, and they are not all equally urgent. Each card below is colour-coded by how quickly it needs attention.

Red, call now Navy, have it investigated Blue, early warning
Call now

Water is overflowing

An overflow relief gully spilling outside, or water rising out of a floor waste, usually means the main line is blocked rather than the fixture. This one is urgent because the next flush has nowhere to go.

Get emergency drain help
Call now

Several drains are out

When the toilet, shower and laundry all back up together, the fault is in the shared sewer line rather than any one fixture. That needs the main line cleared, not a plunger.

Blocked sewer help
Have it investigated

It keeps blocking

A drain that blocks every few months is telling you the pipe is damaged, not dirty. Tree roots in older clay lines are the usual culprit in Sydney, and clearing alone will not stop it.

Tree roots and pipe damage
Have it investigated

There is a bad smell

Sewer odour around the yard or inside can mean a dry trap, a build-up of waste in the line, or a cracked pipe letting gas escape into the soil. A camera tells the three apart quickly.

Book a CCTV inspection
Early warning

It drains slowly

A sink or shower that empties slowly is a partial blockage building up, normally grease and food waste in the kitchen or hair and soap scum in the bathroom. This is the stage where it is simplest to clear, before it closes over completely.

See drain cleaning options
Early warning

The drain gurgles

Gurgling from a sink or toilet is air being pulled past a restriction further down the line. It is an early warning that the blockage is downstream of the fixture, not in the trap.

Common questions

Blocked drain questions, answered

Can you come out today?

We run a 24 hour service and keep capacity aside for genuine emergencies, so ring us and we will tell you honestly when we can be there. For an overflow or a sewage backup, calling (02) 8960 0868 is always faster than an online booking.

Is there really no call-out fee?

Correct. There is no call-out fee to get a licensed plumber to your property and have the drain assessed. Once we have looked at it you get an upfront price for the work, and you decide before anything starts.

What usually causes blocked drains in Sydney homes?

Four causes account for most of them: tree roots getting into older clay pipes, grease and food waste building up in kitchen lines, wet wipes and sanitary items in the sewer, and general debris and silt over time. A CCTV drain inspection tells us which one it is so we treat the cause rather than the symptom.

Will the blockage come back after it is cleared?

If the pipe is structurally sound, a proper clear should last. If the camera shows cracks, a sag or root intrusion, clearing on its own is temporary, and we will talk you through relining or replacing that section so it stops returning.

Can you clear drains for businesses and strata buildings?

Yes. We handle commercial & strata drain cleaning alongside homes, including shared sewer lines across multiple units and scheduled maintenance for cafes, restaurants and larger properties where a blocked drain means downtime.

Which areas of Sydney do you service?

We cover the Sydney metropolitan area across 19 council areas, from the CBD and Inner West through to Parramatta, Blacktown, the Hills, the North Shore, the Eastern Suburbs and the south. Pick your council area above, or browse every suburb we service.
